newsitem.title: MEXICO: Left-winger way ahead in Mexico City race - poll.
newsitem.headline: Left-winger way ahead in Mexico City race - poll.

text.p: Left-wing opposition candidate Cuauhtemoc Cardenas looks set to win a huge victory in Mexico City's mayoral election next month, according to an opinion poll published on Wednesday.
The poll by Reforma newspaper showed Cardenas, the Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) candidate, with 45 percent support, once "don't-knows" and abstentions were excluded.

That was over twice the support of his nearest rival, ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party's (PRI) candidate Alfredo del Mazo. Del Mazo moved up to second place with 22 percent from 21 percent in Reforma's poll a week earlier.
Conservative candidate Carlos Castillo Peraza, of the National Action Party (PAN), slumped to third place with 19 percent, down from 22 percent last week.
The biggest jump in support was for the Green Party candidate, Jorge Gonzalez Torres, whose rating jumped to 10 percent from 7 percent last time.
Reforma said its poll was conducted between June 14 and 15 on a sample of 968 people and had a 3.1 percent margin of error.
The July 6 election will be the first in modern history for mayor of Mexico City. Previous incumbents have been presidential nominees from the ranks of the PRI.
